clips.yt_title: The lost planet gears of the Antikythera mechanism: what the texts describe
clips.claim: Did the Antikythera mechanism display the five planets the Greeks knew?
clips.verdict_from: A display of the five planets? Strong evidence: the texts describe it, but its gears are lost.
clips.summary: Texts on the Antikythera mechanism name all five planets the Greeks knew, each with a pointer and a little sphere, but the gears that moved them are gone. In 2021 a team used two cycles read on the front cover to design sixty-nine gears, more than half of them inferred. The planets are the boldest part of every reconstruction, and the part with the fewest surviving gears.

clips.title: Too advanced|for its *time*?
clips.yt_title: Out of its time, or the survivor of a lost craft? The Antikythera mechanism
clips.claim: Was the Antikythera mechanism too advanced for its time, perhaps a gift from visitors?
clips.verdict_from: A machine out of its time, or from somewhere else? Ruled out: it carries Greek knowledge, and Greek mistakes.
clips.summary: Ancient astronaut books and television shows call the Antikythera mechanism an out-of-place artefact, perhaps a gift from visitors; true, nothing this complex survives again for over a thousand years. But it carries Greek words, a Corinthian calendar, Greek games and Greek astronomy, limits and all. Most ancient bronzes were melted down; this one survived because it sank.

clips.title: How old is|*Stonehenge*?
clips.yt_title: Antler picks, cremations and sarsens: dating Stonehenge stage by stage
clips.claim: Was Stonehenge built in stages by Neolithic farmers, from about 3000 to 1600 BCE?
clips.verdict_from: Built in stages by Neolithic farmers, from about 3000 to 1600 BCE? Established.
clips.summary: Stonehenge began around 3000 BCE as a ring-shaped ditch and bank, dated by the red deer antler picks its diggers left on the floor. The great ring of sarsens and the trilithons came around 2500 BCE, and the bluestones were rearranged until about 1600 BCE. Not one Stonehenge, then, but many, over some fourteen centuries.

clips.title: Who cleared|the *palm forest*?
clips.yt_title: Fire and rats: how Rapa Nui lost its forest of giant palms
clips.claim: Was Rapa Nui's palm forest lost after people arrived, to fire and rats?
clips.verdict_from: A palm forest lost after people came? Established: fire cleared it, rats ate its seeds, and who did more is still argued.
clips.summary: Polynesian voyagers reached Rapa Nui around 1200. Pollen in crater lake mud shows a green island, with perhaps sixteen million giant palms; by the 1500s nearly all were gone. Burned stumps point to people clearing land with fire, and nearly every palm nut found was gnawed by the Polynesian rat. Who did more is still argued.

clips.title: Merlin's stones,|from *Wales*?
clips.yt_title: Merlin's Giants' Dance and the bluestone quarries in the hills of west Wales
clips.claim: Did Stonehenge's bluestones come from quarries in the Preseli Hills of west Wales?
clips.verdict_from: Bluestones from Wales, moved by people, not ice? Strong evidence.
clips.summary: A medieval tale said the wizard Merlin brought Stonehenge from Ireland. In 1923 the geologist Herbert Thomas matched many bluestones to the Preseli Hills of west Wales, and digs at Carn Goedog and Craig Rhos-y-felin found wedges, platforms and hearths from around 3000 BCE. Whether a first Stonehenge stood at Waun Mawn is still debated.

clips.title: Did the moai|*walk*?
clips.yt_title: Did the moai walk? Rocking a four-tonne statue along Rapa Nui's old roads
clips.claim: Were Rapa Nui's moai moved upright, rocked along the roads like walking giants?
clips.verdict_from: Giants that walked upright along the roads? Strong evidence: it fits the statues, the roads and the tests, though no one has walked eighty tonnes.
clips.summary: Almost every moai was carved at one crater, Rano Raraku, and the tallest raised weighed some eighty tonnes. Rapanui tradition says the statues walked. In 2012 eighteen people rocked a four-tonne replica with three ropes, a hundred metres in forty minutes, and the roadside statues and dished roads fit. Nobody has walked eighty tonnes yet.

clips.title: Six tonnes|from *Scotland*?
clips.yt_title: The Altar Stone's journey: how tiny crystals traced it to north-east Scotland
clips.claim: Did Stonehenge's six-tonne Altar Stone come from north-east Scotland?
clips.verdict_from: The Altar Stone, from north-east Scotland? Strong evidence: three studies agree.
clips.summary: Most of Stonehenge's sarsens share one chemistry, pointing to West Woods, about twenty-five kilometres away. The Altar Stone never fitted anywhere. In 2024 tiny mineral grains inside it, dated like stamps in a passport, pointed to north-east Scotland, and in 2026 the closest match turned up in Caithness. By land or by sea, nobody knows yet.

clips.title: Did the island|*collapse* first?
clips.yt_title: A population crash on Rapa Nui before 1722? The dates and gardens, checked
clips.claim: Did Rapa Nui's society crash before any European arrived?
clips.verdict_from: A great crash before the Europeans came? Ruled out: the dates, the gardens and the genes all point the other way.
clips.summary: The 2005 bestseller Collapse called Rapa Nui the clearest example of a society that destroyed itself. But radiocarbon dates from houses and hearths climb until the Europeans arrive, and platforms were still being built after 1722. A 2024 satellite map of rock gardens suggests food for about three thousand people. Critics say it misses some fields.

clips.title: Who moved|the *giants*?
clips.yt_title: Glaciers, sledges or a lost civilisation? How Stonehenge's stones were moved
clips.claim: Were Stonehenge's bluestones moved by people, rather than by Ice Age glaciers?
clips.verdict_from: Bluestones from Wales, moved by people, not ice? Strong evidence.
clips.summary: Since 1971 some geologists have argued that glaciers carried the bluestones. But a boulder once held up as a glacial stray was tied in 2025 to a Welsh quarry, and in 2026 more than five hundred zircon grains showed no sign the ice reached the plain. In a 2016 test, ten people pulled a one-tonne block on a sledge.

clips.title: What do the|*genes* remember?
clips.yt_title: Fifteen Rapanui genomes: steady growth and Native American ancestry
clips.claim: Do Rapanui genomes show contact with Native Americans long before Columbus?
clips.verdict_from: Contact with the Americas, before Columbus? Strong evidence, in the genes.
clips.summary: In 2024, working with Rapanui representatives, a team read the genomes of fifteen people whose remains lay in a Paris museum. They show no population crash in the 1600s, and about a tenth Native American ancestry, mixed in between about 1250 and 1430. Someone crossed the open ocean long before Europeans. The results are helping bring the fifteen home.

clips.title: What was|Stonehenge *for*?
clips.yt_title: Solstice line, calendar, ancestors or feasts: what was Stonehenge for?
clips.claim: Was Stonehenge a place for the dead and for midwinter feasts, built on the solstice line?
clips.verdict_from: A place for the dead, and for midwinter feasts? Strong evidence.
clips.summary: Stonehenge is built on a line: midsummer sunrise one way, midwinter sunset the other, along grooves the Ice Age left in the chalk. A 365-day calendar has been proposed and disputed. Cremations, and pigs brought from as far as Scotland to midwinter feasts at Durrington Walls, point to the dead and the feast. Quite possibly all three, at once.

clips.title: When did the|*collapse* come?
clips.yt_title: Raids, smallpox and a sheep ranch: the collapse that came to Rapa Nui on ships
clips.claim: Did Rapa Nui's population collapse after contact with Europeans and slave raiders?
clips.verdict_from: A collapse after contact? Established: raids and smallpox.
clips.summary: Dutch ships reached Rapa Nui on Easter Sunday, 1722, and found statues still standing. In 1862 slave raiders from Peru took more than fourteen hundred people; the few survivors sent home carried smallpox. By 1877 about a hundred and ten Rapanui were left, and for decades the island was a sheep ranch. There was a collapse. It came on the ships.

clips.title: A script|*invented* here?
clips.yt_title: Rongorongo: was writing invented on Rapa Nui? What a tablet's wood can tell
clips.claim: Was the rongorongo script invented on Rapa Nui before Europeans arrived?
clips.verdict_from: A script invented on the island? Open question.
clips.summary: Rongorongo is a script of tiny signs carved on wooden tablets, every second line upside down. Fewer than thirty pieces survive, and no one can read them yet. In 2024 the wood of one tablet in Rome was dated to a tree felled before the first European ships. But that dates the tree, not the carving, so the question stays open.

clips.title: Pyramids laid out|like *Orion*?
clips.yt_title: Orion's Belt and the Giza pyramids: how close is the likeness?
clips.claim: Were the three Giza pyramids laid out to copy the three stars of Orion's Belt?
clips.verdict_from: A plan copied from Orion's Belt? Open question. The likeness is real, and Egypt looked to Orion.
clips.summary: Robert Bauval saw the Giza plan in Orion's Belt: two big pyramids on one line and a smaller one stepped aside, like the faint star Mintaka. He set out the idea in 1989 and, with Adrian Gilbert, in the 1994 book The Orion Mystery. A 2026 statistical study found the likeness is real. The question is what it means.

clips.title: A river|of *villages*?
clips.yt_title: Orellana's voyage down the Amazon and the friar who saw villages on its banks
clips.claim: Were the Amazon's banks lined with big villages when Europeans first sailed down the river?
clips.verdict_from: Carvajal's crowded banks? Strong evidence: big villages on the high banks, with empty stretches between, much as he said.
clips.summary: In 1541 a Spanish army marched east from Quito chasing the story of El Dorado, and found hunger instead. Francisco de Orellana's men followed the river all the way to the Atlantic, and their chaplain, Gaspar de Carvajal, wrote of village after village on the high banks. Later travellers found empty river, and many read his account as a tall tale.

clips.title: A sky from|*10,500 BCE*?
clips.yt_title: Does Giza record the sky of 10,500 BCE? The lean of Orion's Belt, checked
clips.claim: Does the Giza plan record the sky as it was around 10,500 BCE?
clips.verdict_from: And a map of the sky of ten thousand, five hundred BCE? Awaiting evidence. The claimed match misses by about ten degrees.
clips.summary: Earth wobbles like a top, so over the millennia Orion's Belt crosses the sky over Giza higher or lower. In The Orion Mystery, Bauval and Gilbert dated the match to around 10,450 BCE. Astronomers note the sky must be turned nearly upside down, and in 1999 Anthony Fairall found that the belt then leaned about ten degrees off the pyramids' line.

clips.title: A lost city|called *Z*?
clips.yt_title: Percy Fawcett's lost city of Z and the earthen towns of the Upper Xingu
clips.claim: Was there a lost city of stone in the forests where Percy Fawcett vanished in 1925?
clips.verdict_from: El Dorado, or Fawcett's Z: cities of gold, or of stone? Awaiting evidence. But towns of earth stood where both were sought.
clips.summary: In 1925 the explorer Percy Fawcett went into the forests of Mato Grosso to find a lost city he called Z, and never came back. Some seventy years later, archaeologists working with the Kuikuro people mapped ditches, plazas and straight roads under the Upper Xingu forest, mostly from 1250 to 1650 CE. Fawcett looked for stone. The towns were made of earth.

clips.title: Shafts aimed|at the *stars*?
clips.yt_title: The Great Pyramid's shafts: aimed at Orion's Belt, or simple builders' slopes?
clips.claim: Were the Great Pyramid's shafts aimed at the stars of the builders' own age?
clips.verdict_from: Shafts aimed at the stars of that age, a road for the king's spirit? Plausible. Simple builders' slopes could explain their angles too.
clips.summary: Two narrow shafts leave the King's Chamber of the Great Pyramid. In 1964 Alexander Badawy and Virginia Trimble found the southern one framed Orion's Belt around 2500 BCE. Measured again in the 1990s, the shafts point to stars of around 2450 BCE, the age archaeologists give the building. But forty-five degrees is also the simplest slope to set.

clips.title: Could the forest|*feed* a city?
clips.yt_title: Terra preta and a forest of planted trees: the Amazon as a cultivated paradise
clips.claim: Did Amazonians make their own fertile dark earth, terra preta?
clips.verdict_from: Dark earth made by people? Established.
clips.summary: In 1971 Betty Meggers called the Amazon a counterfeit paradise: poor soils, she argued, capped how many people the forest could feed. But patches of black earth, terra preta, built up over centuries around old villages, and the Kuikuro still make dark earth on purpose. Even the trees carry the mark: domesticated kinds like the Brazil nut are among the commonest.

clips.title: Who built|*Giza*, and when?
clips.yt_title: Merer's diary, charcoal dates and a workers' town: who built Giza, and when
clips.claim: Were the three Giza pyramids built by Khufu, his son and his grandson, about 4,500 years ago?
clips.verdict_from: Three pyramids built by Khufu, his son and his grandson, about four and a half thousand years ago: established.
clips.summary: Charcoal in the pyramids' mortar, dated in 1984 and 1995, came out older than the history books by one to four centuries, but nowhere near 10,000 BCE. At a Red Sea harbour, Pierre Tallet's team found the diary of an inspector named Merer, ferrying limestone to the Horizon of Khufu. South of the Sphinx lies the town where the builders worked.

clips.title: What did lidar|find in *Bolivia*?
clips.yt_title: Lidar in the Llanos de Mojos: the Casarabe towns, causeways and reservoirs
clips.claim: Did the Casarabe culture build planned towns with causeways and reservoirs in the Bolivian Amazon?
clips.verdict_from: Planned towns in the Amazon, with platforms, causeways and reservoirs, long before Europeans? Established: mapped, dug and dated.
clips.summary: In 2019 a team flew lidar over the Llanos de Mojos, a Bolivian floodplain where the Casarabe culture lived from about 500 to 1400 CE. Two great towns appeared, ringed by moats and ramparts, with a cone of earth twenty-two metres tall at Cotoca, and straight raised causeways, canals and reservoirs. The towns faded around 1400, before any European arrived.

clips.title: Did Egypt|look to *Orion*?
clips.yt_title: Sah, the king's star: what the Pyramid Texts say about Orion and the pyramids
clips.claim: Do Egyptian texts tie the three Giza pyramids to the three stars of Orion's Belt?
clips.verdict_from: A plan copied from Orion's Belt? Open question. The likeness is real, and Egypt looked to Orion.
clips.summary: Around 2350 BCE, carvers covered the burial chamber of King Unas with the Pyramid Texts. They speak of Sah, the Egyptian name for Orion, linked with Osiris, and greet the king as a companion of Orion. Many Egyptologists think the Great Pyramid's shafts were a road for the king's spirit. But no text yet found matches the pyramids to the stars.

clips.title: A valley of|*straight* roads?
clips.yt_title: The Upano valley and Acre's geoglyphs: lidar keeps finding more in the Amazon
clips.claim: Did the Upano valley in Ecuador hold planned towns linked by roads dug dead straight?
clips.verdict_from: Planned towns in the Amazon, with platforms, causeways and reservoirs, long before Europeans? Established: mapped, dug and dated.
clips.summary: In 2024 Stephen Rostain's team published a lidar map of the Upano valley in Ecuador: more than six thousand platforms round low plazas, and roads dug dead straight across the valley. In Brazil's Acre state, a 2026 lidar study found 432 earthworks along its flight lines, where 36 were known. How many people lived here is still an open question.

clips.title: A people known|from a *fingertip*?
clips.yt_title: A finger bone from Denisova Cave and the DNA of a people nobody knew
clips.claim: Were the Denisovans a distinct human group, known first from the DNA of one finger bone?
clips.verdict_from: A distinct human group, known first from its DNA, whose genes live on in us? Established.
clips.summary: In 2008 a chip of finger bone came out of Denisova Cave, in the Altai Mountains of Siberia. About seventy percent of its DNA was the girl's own, and by 2010 her genome revealed cousins of the Neanderthals, on a branch of their own: the Denisovans. A whole human group, known from its DNA before anyone had seen its face.

clips.title: Two peoples,|*one* girl?
clips.yt_title: Denny: the girl with a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father
clips.claim: Did a girl from Denisova Cave have a Neanderthal mother and a Denisovan father?
clips.verdict_from: Sets up: A distinct human group, known first from its DNA, whose genes live on in us? Established.
clips.summary: In 2012 a scrap of bone from Denisova Cave went into a bag with thousands of splinters. Screened by its collagen, it turned out to be human, and in 2018 its genome showed one copy Neanderthal and the other Denisovan. Her mother was a Neanderthal, her father a Denisovan. When these peoples met, they had children.

clips.title: Denisovan genes|*in us*?
clips.yt_title: Denisovan DNA in people today, from Papua New Guinea to the Tibetan Plateau
clips.claim: Do people alive today carry Denisovan DNA, including a gene that helps Tibetans live high up?
clips.verdict_from: A distinct human group, known first from its DNA, whose genes live on in us? Established.
clips.summary: Millions of people alive today carry Denisovan DNA: four to six parts in a hundred in some people in Papua New Guinea, even more among the Ayta Magbukon of the Philippines, and a trace across mainland Asia. Most Tibetans carry a version of a gene that keeps their blood from thickening up high, traced in 2014 to the Denisovans or people very like them.

clips.title: Who lived on the|*roof* of the world?
clips.yt_title: A jaw from a Tibetan cave: how proteins and DNA in the dirt found Denisovans
clips.claim: Did Denisovans live high on the Tibetan Plateau, long before our own species arrived?
clips.verdict_from: The jaws from Tibet and Taiwan? Strong evidence, from their proteins.
clips.summary: In 1980 a Buddhist monk found half of a human jaw in a cave 3,280 metres up on the Tibetan Plateau. No DNA survived, but in 2019 proteins from one of its teeth matched the Denisovans. Denisovan DNA later turned up in the cave's dirt, with the bones of what they butchered: blue sheep, wild yaks, woolly rhinos. They lived with thin air long before us.

clips.title: Is this a|*Denisovan* face?
clips.yt_title: Dragon Man: is the Harbin skull the first Denisovan face?
clips.claim: Is the Harbin skull, nicknamed Dragon Man, the face of a Denisovan?
clips.verdict_from: The Harbin skull as a Denisovan face? Strong evidence, with a few careful sceptics.
clips.summary: In 1933 a man building a railway bridge in Harbin, China, dug up a human skull and, his family says, hid it in a well. Its describers called it a new species, nicknamed Dragon Man. In 2025 a Beijing team recovered proteins and a trace of DNA that point to the Denisovans. Not everyone is convinced: one skull may not speak for a whole people.

clips.title: Were they|*giants*?
clips.yt_title: Were the Denisovans giants? Two leg bones from the Taiwan Strait, measured
clips.claim: Were the Denisovans giants, as you often read online?
clips.verdict_from: Giants? Awaiting evidence. No bone points there.
clips.summary: Online, you often read that the Denisovans were giants, and their bones are big. Two leg bones from the Taiwan Strait, with a Denisovan protein marker, suggest people about one metre eighty and one metre ninety tall, in a 2026 study not yet peer reviewed. Tall, like a tall person today. And a big tooth tells you about chewing, not height.
